provenance.note: Curated compilation; per-record citations carry the accountability. Indian Kanoon is the mirror used for court and tribunal orders; the court, case number and date are the citation.

note: Nagpur's lake record is spread across four kinds of official document that do not always agree: NMC's Environment Status Reports (progress as informed by NMC), the State's Government Resolutions (sanctions and releases), the AMRUT 2.0 portal (the Centre's milestones) and NMC's budgets (each year's money). Where they give different costs or stages for the same lake, all are shown with the document each comes from. Court and tribunal orders were read on Indian Kanoon; the court, case number and date are the citation, and orders that recite press reports are carried for their directions only. Press reports were used as leads, never as figures.

projects.scheme_name: AMRUT 2.0 lake rejuvenation: Naik and Lendi
projects.scope: Two lakes sanctioned on 2 November 2022, each to be completed in 12 months: Naik (desilting, storm drain, sewer line, edge wall, toilet block, yoga shed, compound wall, immersion tank) and Lendi. The AMRUT 2.0 portal lists Naik as 'Project Completed'. NMC's 2023-24 report records Lendi's work as not completed because of opposition from residents to the removal of encroachments.
projects.funding_summary: Sanctions: Naik Rs 12.95 crore (Centre 3.24, State 3.24, NMC 6.48) and Lendi Rs 14.13 crore (3.53, 3.53, 7.07). The portal lists only Naik, at Rs 15.95 crore. NMC's 2022-23 report mentions Rs 1.5 crore sought for Naik, Mangalwari and Lendi lakes under AMRUT 2.0; the sanctions are the figures used here. The two GRs' text was read from the orgpedia mahGRs archive copy (the official PDFs did not open on 15 October 2026).

projects.financier: State basic-amenities grants, the 15th Finance Commission and AMRUT 2.0, per NMC's reports
projects.scope: NMC's 2023-24 report: first phase complete at Gandhisagar, Sakkardara, Sonegaon and Naik, and work complete at Police Line Takli and Binaki; Gandhisagar, Sakkardara and Sonegaon 'under 2nd phase of development and beautification', including desilting, walking tracks, rainwater drains, edge and retaining walls, toilet blocks, sewage treatment plants, fountains, footbridges and parking.
projects.funding_summary: NMC's 2022-23 report records that NMC 'dedicated a huge surplus of Rs 100 crore' to Gandhisagar, Sonegaon and Sakkardara, 'to be completed by 2024'. The report cites no sanction order for the figure.

projects.financier: Government of Maharashtra: Urban Development (phase 1) and Tourism and Cultural Affairs (phase 2)
projects.scope: Phase 1: retaining walls on the south and north, a garden, shops, an amphitheatre, a footpath and recharge shafts. Phase 2: works on the south, west and east sides to make the lake a tourist destination.
projects.funding_summary: Phase 1 Rs 17.32 crore (sanctioned 28 February 2019); phase 2 Rs 24.96 crore (7 November 2023, with Rs 8.25 crore released and the money to be spent by 31 March 2024). NMC's 2026-27 budget provides Rs 12 crore (Rs 1,200 lakh) for the project.

projects.scope: Development and beautification of the old Bhonsle-era tank in the city centre; first phase complete and second phase under way in 2023-24, per NMC's report.
projects.funding_summary: NMC's budgets carry Rs 1 crore a year as NMC's share of the lake's rejuvenation (Rs 100 lakh in both 2025-26 and 2026-27). No State sanction order for the lake was found among the Government Resolutions indexed by department, so the project's total cost is not shown.

projects.financier: Government of Maharashtra (100%), special provision for basic amenities in municipal corporation areas
projects.scope: Permissible development works at Sakkardara lake; the Collector to give administrative approval for each work.

projects.operator: Maha Metro and the Nagpur Improvement Trust
projects.scope: A musical fountain, a viewers' gallery, a parking plaza and floating structures (a restaurant, a banquet hall and an artificial banyan tree). The High Court declined to order their removal but barred any permanent construction within the lake (30 November 2023); the Supreme Court upheld this on 7 October 2025. Before the Tribunal, the lake's ownership is stated to vest in the State Public Works Department.
projects.funding_summary: No cost is stated in any official document read.
projects.status: Upheld by the Supreme Court (2025); Tribunal case open

projects.scheme_name: Ambazari dam safety works and the Nag widening
projects.operator: NMC (the dam's owner), the State Water Resources and Public Works Departments, and Maha Metro
projects.scope: A State High Level Committee (5 January 2024) to complete the works to strengthen the dam; three spillway gates of 4 m by 2.5 m, whose design the Irrigation Department reported in progress (February 2024); a high-level submersible bridge across the spill; and widening the Nag from 14 m to 18 m at Crazy Castle below the dam.
projects.funding_summary: NMC's 2025-26 budget: Rs 11 crore (Rs 1,100 lakh) for strengthening the dam. State Disaster Mitigation Fund: Rs 19.84 crore to Maha Metro for the Nag widening (7 May 2025). The two are separate sanctions and are not added up.

projects.scheme_name: Artificial idol-immersion tanks and lake upkeep
projects.financier: Government of Maharashtra grant (Rs 31.90 crore received)
projects.scope: Three artificial tanks for public idol immersion: at Gorewada village (estimated Rs 19.62 crore), Kachhi Visa ground (estimated Rs 2.15 crore) and Police Line Takli lake (estimated Rs 8.50 crore). All three were complete and used in Ganeshotsav 2025.
projects.funding_summary: Rs 30.27 crore approved by the Collector from the State grant. NMC's 2026-27 budget also provides Rs 4 crore (Rs 400 lakh) for maintenance, repair and environmental works at the city's lakes.

court_orders.case: Swacch Association, Nagpur v. State of Maharashtra, 2025 INSC 1199
court_orders.writ_petition: Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) 1420/2024
court_orders.ruling: dismissed the appeal. It held that Futala, which it records was built in 1799 as a man-made tank for irrigation and drinking water, is not a 'wetland' under the Wetlands Rules, 2017, and upheld the High Court's directions that no permanent structure be built within the lake and that the water body be kept clean. It held that the public trust doctrine extends to man-made water bodies.
court_orders.concern: the lakefront's fountain, gallery and floating structures

court_orders.case: Swacch Association, Nagpur v. State of Maharashtra (2023:BHC-NAG:16604-DB)
court_orders.ruling: declined to order removal of the musical fountain, viewers' gallery and parking plaza, directed that no construction of a permanent nature be undertaken within Futala lake, and directed Maha Metro and NMC to ensure their activities do not damage the lake and to keep the water body clean and properly maintained.

court_orders.case: In re: news item on Futala Lake (suo motu)
court_orders.court: National Green Tribunal, Western Zone Bench
court_orders.ruling: has heard the case since June 2025. A joint committee of CPCB, MPCB and NMC reported that about 145-160 houses beside the lake have no sewer and that the settlement has 8 cow shelters (gaushalas), and made seven recommendations; on 18 November 2025 the Tribunal asked NMC for an action plan with a timeline. On 10 September 2026 NMC reported a technical sanction of Rs 33,09,488 and a budget provision of Rs 36,24,426 for a sewer, and MPCB was asked whether CPCB's guidelines for dairy farms and gaushalas are followed. The case was next listed for 29 October 2026.
court_orders.concern: a newspaper report on the condition of the lake

court_orders.case: Public interest litigation on the Ambazari overflow of September 2023
court_orders.ruling: has overseen Ambazari's safety works since December 2023: it directed NMC and the Nagpur Improvement Trust to remove structures obstructing the Nag (17 January 2024), asked the State's High Level Committee to complete temporary flood-safety measures before the 2024 monsoon (8 May 2024), and recorded the Irrigation Department's affidavit that the design of three spillway gates was in progress and the need for the Nag below the dam to carry at least 75 cumecs (11 July 2024). On 2 July 2025 it recorded that the dam's safety is NMC's responsibility as its owner.
court_orders.concern: the flood of 23 September 2023 below Ambazari dam, in which the Collector's affidavit records four deaths

court_orders.case: Court on its own motion v. State of Maharashtra (city lakes) (2026:BHC-NAG:7264-DB)
court_orders.ruling: disposed of the case with directions to the District Collector and the NMC Commissioner to look into the issue, conduct the necessary enquiry, take the steps essential for conserving the city's lakes, and submit an action-taken report to the Registrar (Judicial) within four months.
court_orders.concern: newspaper reports on the degradation of several lakes in the city

court_orders.case: Court on its own motion v. State of Maharashtra (Sonegaon lake)
court_orders.ruling: issued notice to the State, NMC and the Nagpur Improvement Trust, returnable on 24 December 2025, and appointed an amicus curiae.
court_orders.concern: backwater from the lake entering homes

court_orders.case: Court on its own motion v. State of Maharashtra (Ambazari lake)
court_orders.ruling: took on record NEERI's report on the lake's water and asked NMC to report within three weeks on removing the high concentration of phytoplankton, with a programme for periodic cleaning and for desilting.

court_orders.case: Nagpur Municipal Corporation v. State of Maharashtra
court_orders.ruling: stayed directions on Ambazari's safety issued by the Maharashtra Water Resources Regulatory Authority on 10 December 2020, holding prima facie that the Authority lacked jurisdiction, and recorded that PIL 96/2017, disposed of on 21 March 2018, had already given comprehensive directions on the dam.
court_orders.concern: the Water Resources Regulatory Authority's directions on the dam's safety

court_orders.case: In re: news item on a high-rise near Ambazari lake (suo motu)
court_orders.court: National Green Tribunal, Western Zone Bench
court_orders.ruling: disposed of the case without directions, recording the permissions the building held and that it stands higher than the top of the spillway, and that the flood question is before the High Court in PIL 56/2023.
court_orders.concern: a newspaper report on flood risk from a high-rise building beside Ambazari lake

court_orders.case: Court on its own motion v. State of Maharashtra (Vidarbha river pollution)
court_orders.ruling: recorded NMC's statement that it had appointed contractors and service providers for 11 lakes and 3 rivers, with a project report for each.
court_orders.concern: pollution of rivers and lakes in Vidarbha
